  -', '- 1
  - ', '- 1

findings.summary: wrappedList relaxes the empty-bullet-interrupts-paragraph restriction for '-', '*', and '+' markers, but tests only cover '-'
findings.evidence: isEmptyBulletLine (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts) treats DASH, '*' (0x2a) and '+' (0x2b) all as qualifying 'empty bullet' markers, and wrappedList applies the paragraph-interrupt override uniformly to all three. Only the '-' variant is needed to fix the setext-heading collision (only '-' is ambiguous with a setext underline); '*'/'+' never trigger lheadingRule at all, so allowing them to interrupt a paragraph is an additional CommonMark deviation. None of the new tests in preview.test.ts use '*' or '+' bullets, so this broader behavior change ships with zero coverage.

findings.summary: listEmptyBulletPlugin reaches into markdown-it's private Ruler internals (`ruler.__rules__`) to read the current `list` rule function, rather than using any public API. This is undocumented, version-fragile behavior: a markdown-it patch/minor bump that renames or restructures `__rules__` (or changes `Ruler.at`'s alt-clearing semantics) would silently break note rendering for every user, and nothing in the diff or its tests would catch that until it manifests as a runtime TypeError or a rendering regression, since `getRuleFn` throws at plugin-install time (module load) rather than being typed against a stable contract.
findings.evidence: function getRuleFn(md: MarkdownIt, name: string): BlockRule { const ruler = md.block.ruler as unknown as { __rules__: Array<{ name: string; fn: BlockRule; enabled: boolean }> }; ... }

findings.summary: Checked for blast radius beyond the single `md` singleton in preview.ts: markdown-it is instantiated exactly once in the whole repo (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts), NotePreview is only consumed by packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts, and no other module queries preview output for headings/TOC or otherwise depends on the changed lheading/list block-rule behavior. The rule replacements themselves correctly restore the `list` rule's original `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` chain (matching upstream) and leave `lheading`'s alt chain untouched, which matches upstream's own empty alt for that rule, so no other plugin registered earlier (task-lists, katex, details-plugin) loses its terminator membership. No bypass or broken caller found; noting this as an explicit negative result rather than a gap.
Lone single-dash setext H2 headings (a valid, common CommonMark pattern, e.g. `Heading\n-`) are now broken anywhere in the document, not just inside nested lists as intended.
findings.evidence:
`isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1` is applied unconditionally in `lheadingRule`, with no check that we are actually inside a list item (i.e. no check of nesting/parentType beyond the generic 'paragraph' terminator convention that also fires at the top level). For input like `Heading\n-` (a legal single-dash setext H2, per CommonMark and how e.g. the reference dingus renders it), `isLoneDash` is true, so `level` is never set and the loop falls through to the terminatorRules check for that same line. Because the dash line also satisfies `isEmptyBulletLine` (bare `-` with nothing after), the wrapped `list` rule (line ~186-197) reports it as a paragraph terminator even though we are not nested under any list. The paragraph 'Heading' is then closed early and the standalone `-` line is parsed non-silently by the normal `list` rule (now that `parentType` is no longer `'paragraph'`), producing a spurious empty `
` instead of `

Heading

`. Only `Heading\n---` (multi-dash) is covered by the new test suite; the single-dash case is untested and regresses standard setext-heading rendering.

findings.summary: isEmptyBulletLine has no upper-bound indentation check, unlike the code-block threshold used elsewhere (lheadingRule and markdown-it's real list rule), so an over-indented dash (which CommonMark would treat as an indented code block / lazy continuation, not a list marker) can still be misclassified as an 'empty bullet' terminator.
findings.evidence: `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent` (too little indent) but never checks the upper bound (`state.sCount[line] - state.blkIndent >= 4`), which both `lheadingRule` (line 63) and markdown-it's actual `list` rule apply before treating a marker as a valid list start. A dash indented 4+ spaces past blkIndent would normally be an indented-code/lazy-continuation line that should NOT terminate the enclosing paragraph, but the wrapped `list` rule's silent short-circuit (line ~186) will still claim it terminates the paragraph, diverging from the delegate `originalList`'s own (correct) behavior for that same input.

findings.summary: getRuleFn hard-throws by reaching into markdown-it's private `__rules__` array at plugin-registration time (module load), with no fallback if that internal shape ever changes in a future markdown-it patch/minor release (dependency is pinned with a caret range `^14.1.0`).
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` throws `Error('markdown-it block rule not found: list')` if `ruler.__rules__` doesn't contain a `list` entry with that private shape; this is called unconditionally from `listEmptyBulletPlugin`, which itself runs at module-eval time in `preview.ts` (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)`), so an incompatible markdown-it version would crash the entire notes preview module on import rather than degrading gracefully to the stock `list` behavior.
searchedFor: node_modules markdown-it internals (not installed in this checkout, could not directly verify current stability)

verdict.reason:
Traced the code path directly. `lheadingRule` (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105) computes `isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1` unconditionally — there is no check for whether the current heading candidate is nested inside a list (no check of list depth/`state.listIndent`, only the generic `state.parentType === 'paragraph'` flag that markdown-it sets during *any* paragraph/lheading terminator scan, top-level or nested alike). For top-level input `Heading -`: lheadingRule sets `state.parentType='paragraph'` (line 77), scans to line 1, sets `isLoneDash=true`, so `level` is never assigned (line 107-110 skipped) and the loop falls through to the terminatorRules check (line 118-126), which calls the wrapped `list` rule silently; `wrappedList` (lines 181-193) sees `silent && parentType==='paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(...)` all true and returns `true`, terminating the scan — but since `level` is still 0, `lheadingRule` returns `false` (line 129-132) regardless of that terminate signal. Control falls through to the stock `paragraph` rule, which independently re-runs the same terminator check via the same `wrappedList`, closing the paragraph `Heading` at line 1. The tokenizer then starts a fresh top-level block at line 1 with `silent=false` and `state.parentType` no longer `'paragraph'`, so `wrappedList` falls through to `originalList(state, 1, endLine, false)` — the stock, unmodified `list` rule — which (per CommonMark, since it is not being asked to interrupt a paragraph in this non-silent top-level call) happily builds an empty `
` from the lone `-`. Result: `

Heading

` instead of the CommonMark-mandated `

Heading

` (single-dash setext underlines are explicitly valid per the CommonMark spec's list-items section, precisely because an empty list item cannot interrupt a paragraph — the same rule this plugin exploits, but applied without restricting to nested-list context). Confirmed via preview.test.ts (lines 151-187): only the nested case (`'- 1 -'`, `'- 1 - '`) and the multi-dash setext case (`'Heading ---'`) are tested; the top-level single-dash setext case the reviewer describes is not covered anywhere, and no guard in the file restricts the `isLoneDash` special-case to nested-list contexts.
